title: Throwing a Ball on the Moon
learningObjectives: Describe drag-free ballistic flight with constant horizontal speed and vertically decelerated motion
Calculate horizontal position as x = U0 * t and vertical motion from V = V0 - g * t
Calculate maximum height as ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g) and explain higher throws where g is smaller

sources.title: Throwing a ball on the Moon (project-authored test text)
sources.attribution: Written by the Make knowledge interactive project team for testing.

evidence.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

explanations.text: On the Moon with no air there is no drag, so flight is purely ballistic with weight pulling straight down.

evidence.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight
and the ball moves x = U0 * t across the ground.

explanations.text: With no sideways push the horizontal speed stays U0, so distance across the ground grows as x = U0 * t.

evidence.quote: The ball stops rising when V = 0, which happens at t = V0 / g.
Putting that time into the height equation gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

explanations.text: The ball stops rising at t = V0 / g, giving peak height ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g), much higher where g is small.

predictions.prompt: A ball is thrown on the airless Moon with horizontal speed 12 m/s and vertical speed 8 m/s under Moon gravity 1.62 m/s^2. What is the maximum height?
